text:
I grew up amid a populated silence

inside the cold cradle of the newborn century.

Human voices did not touch me.

It was the voices of the wind I heard.

I gave my favors to burdocks and weeds,

but what was most precious to me was the silver willow,

great companion through the years,

whose weeping branches

quickened my insomnia with dreams.

Unbelievably I have survived:

outside only a severed trunk remains. Now other

willows

recite under our skies

with alienated voices.

And I remain silent, as if I had lost a brother.




1940

translation.title: I Grew Up amid a Populated Silence...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the silver willow as companion, survivor, and lost brother.
